svg.title: Figure 9-2. Threat scenes: the risk-5 threat scenarios (WP-C-09 §9)
svg.desc: One card per threat scenario, the risk-5 threat scenarios: TS-02 A compromised SoC switches the panda to a permissive safety mode; TS-03 A compromised SoC puts other firmware on the panda; TS-04 Forged parameters or messages on the SoC bend the plan or mute monitoring; TS-11 A stolen device exposes driver video, trips and its identity key; TS-14 A compromised SoC sends camera frames or floods actuation via the panda.
svg.text: Figure 9-2. Threat scenes: the risk-5 threat scenarios

Each card: where the threat sits in the risk matrix; what the damage looks like (schematic, loops every 6 s); how it gets there at the §5 level, with the missing control in red; what the item trusts; the feasibility factors and impact ratings.
Ratings, paths, risk and treatment from WP-C-09, goals from WP-C-10, in the order of the §9 top-risk table. No exploitation detail: the cards stay at the abstraction of §5.

g.title: TS-02: A compromised SoC switches the panda to a permissive safety mode
g.text: A compromised SoC switches the panda
WHAT THE DAMAGE LOOKS LIKE · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
Foothold: code runs on the SoC
Panda told to use another safety mode
Envelope gone: a full-torque swerve passes
HOW IT GETS THERE · THE MISSING CONTROL IN RED

svg.text: Code execution on the SoC (QM user space)

g.text: “Any safety-mode command from the SoC is
The safety-mode command has no authentication or cross-check,
so code on the SoC can swap the envelope out. The reference
build now locks the mode in firmware; not yet verified, and
FEASIBILITY FACTORS (§6, AP-02) · DARKER = EASIER FOR THE ATTACKER
→ feasibility High; knowledge is public on every path (open source)
IMPACT (§3, HIGHEST OVER THE DAMAGE SCENARIOS)

g.title: TS-03: A compromised SoC puts other firmware on the panda
g.text: A compromised SoC puts other firmware
WHAT THE DAMAGE LOOKS LIKE · SCHEMATIC, LOOPS EVERY 6 S
Foothold: code runs on the SoC
The panda boot path loads other firmware
HOW IT GETS THERE · THE MISSING CONTROL IN RED

svg.text: Code execution on the SoC (QM user space)
SoC reprograms the panda via its boot path

g.text: “Only signed firmware ever runs on the safety
With code on the SoC, its control of the panda boot path can
put other firmware on the MCU, and flash protection is not yet
in place to stop it. The envelope is then whatever that
firmware does. Details: private record GD-03.
FEASIBILITY FACTORS (§6, AP-03) · DARKER = EASIER FOR THE ATTACKER
→ feasibility High; knowledge is public on every path (open source)
IMPACT (§3, HIGHEST OVER THE DAMAGE SCENARIOS)

g.text: “Every parameter and message comes from the
Parameters are plain files and inter-process messages carry no
authentication, so any local process can change the plan, the
model output or driver monitoring. The panda bounds the
